text:
alex: Heads up — saw a weird spike at ~18:15 UTC. Hosted requests from US paid tier are being routed to eu-west variants and exhausting reserved quota there :rotating_light:

mira: Wait, cross-region fallback for US customers? we have a rule to prefer same-region unless unavailable

alex: Yep, timeline: some US nodes reported transient OOMs and started replying with 503->smart-router started fallback to eu variants, but eu variants are lower-capacity for that tenant so we hit quota-throttle and started 429 fanout back to other regions

kyle: That sounds like a fallback amplification loop — router falls back -> target rate-limits -> router considers target unhealthy -> spreads more -> repeat

jen: Any quick mitigations? Can we stop cross-region fallbacks for "paid" tier until we fix routing policy?

mira: We can toggle the per-tier cross-region fallback flag in runtime config. Suggest flip it off and pin routing to origin-region for paid tiers.

alex: I'm going to post the console link with traces: https://console.redwood/*/routes/trace?trace_id=tx-9f3a

ops-bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-1805-routing-loop - severity=P2 - assigned to eng-platform

kyle: Quick config snippet to disable cross-region fallback for paid tier:

```json
{
  "routing_policy": {
    "tier_overrides": {
      "paid": { "allow_cross_region_fallback": false }
    }
  }
}
```

mira: alex, can you run the runtime flip? curl against the config API:

```bash
curl -XPOST https://config.redwood/api/v1/runtime-flags \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"feature.routing.disable_cross_region_for_paid": true}'
```

alex: Running now. Applying to primary clusters first (us-east/us-west), then monitor.

deploy-bot: rollout-started: feature.routing.disable_cross_region_for_paid -> canary on us-east -> request_id=r-4521

jen: Also add a guard on fallback to prefer variant capacity check before failover. Current check only looks at last-5xx count, not quota headroom.

kyle: Agreed — we need to change the fallback heuristic to include target.available_capacity > min_capacity_threshold. I'll open a patch after we stabilize the emergency flag.

alex: Flip applied on us-east. Observability: cost-by-region graph shows immediate drop in cross-region egress. 429s from eu drop too :thumbsup:

mira: Nice. Can you keep the flag on for 30m and then toggle for us-west if stable?

alex: Will do. Leaving canary for 10m, then propagate.

ops-bot: update: INC-2026-1805-routing-loop severity reduced to P3 — mitigation in place

kyle: Post-mortem notes to capture:
- fallback decision path didn't account for per-variant reserved_quota
- rate limit responses (429) weren't treated as terminal for fallback logic -> caused widen/flip behavior
- console lacked a per-tenant cross-region egress heatmap for quick debugging

jen: I'll add a short UX card to Console backlog: show cross-region fallbacks and a one-click emergency toggle per tier.

mira: For runtime/infra fix I'll propose:
1) fallback requires (available_capacity >= 2x request_batch_estimate) OR explicit override
2) treat 429 from variant as 'do_not_route_here' for N seconds for that tenant
3) telemetry: emit fallback_path tags on traces so we can filter in console dashboards

alex: + create an alert: if >5% of paid-tier requests are routed cross-region in 5m window, page oncall.

deploy-bot: rollout-succeeded: feature.routing.disable_cross_region_for_paid -> global after canary -> id=r-4521 -> duration=12m

alex: After global flip: 503/429 cascade stopped. Slow steady backlog clearing.

jen: Follow-ups: add unit tests to routing simulation harness to simulate variant headroom exhaustion and ensure no amplification loop.

kyle: I'll draft the PR for the heuristic change and add simulation tests.

mira: Great coordination — let's add this incident to the monthly reliability review.

alex: Thanks team. Adding links: traces: https://console.redwood/*/trace/tx-9f3a, dashboard: https://console.redwood/*/dash/egress-by-region

jen: small note — consider an admin-only console action that temporarily routes traffic away from a specific variant (not whole region). Could be useful to drain a buggy model variant without blocking fallback entirely.

kyle: good idea. we'll model as "variant_quarantine" action in routing API.

alex: Closing thread once post-mortem is in. :white_check_mark:
